action: General advice: port users and shippers should rely only on channels announced by the Autoridade Portuária de Santos, and treat unexpected emails or calls about cargo, access or payments with caution.
date_note: Systems went down on 6 November; the ransom contact was reported on 17 November by O POVO, the date first used here.
exec: Brazil's largest port authority is still running many systems in alternative mode after a cyberattack; APS says cargo handling was never compromised.
impact: More than 30 systems running in alternative mode as of 18 November (ABC do ABC); SAP and SDD partly back for staff. About 70% of file backups recovered by 12 November (Gazeta do Povo). APS says no confidential data leaked.
plain: The authority running Brazil's Port of Santos is still running many systems in alternative mode after a cyberattack on 6 November. Federal Police are investigating; APS says cargo handling was never compromised.

key_findings: Baguete (10 Nov): APS confirmed a cyberattack on port systems, down since the morning of 6 Nov; it first cited a power outage hitting its servers and had not determined scale or whether data was accessed.
Cesportos raised the port protection level to II; the Federal Police office in Santos said it had been notified but had received no documents or opened an inquiry.

O POVO (17 Nov): APS confirmed it received a ransom demand from hackers claiming the attack; preliminary investigation points to action from outside Brazil; a report is being prepared for the Federal Police.
APS says data was kept in backups and is being recovered, and believes the virus had been present since at least 6 Nov.

Revista Oeste (12 Nov, relaying APS president Anderson Pomini via Metropoles): a group that claimed the attack tried to negotiate a ransom, got no reply and no terms were set; APS has not confirmed a criminal intrusion; about 70% of affected files recovered from backups; Federal Police opened an inquiry on Tuesday (the article gives no date).

Gazeta do Povo (13 Nov): Federal Police opened an inquiry on Tuesday 10 Nov; hackers emailed APS saying they had breached its systems and asking it to make contact, APS did not respond; about 70% of file backups recovered by 12 Nov; APS website restored early 13 Nov.

ABC do ABC (18 Nov): more than 30 systems still run in alternative mode; SAP and SDD partly back; APS technical report cites a power failure that shut the datacenters followed by a cyber intrusion that erased data; APS says no confidential data leaked; incident investigated by the Federal Police.

summary: Santos Port Authority (APS) systems went down on 6 November. Gazeta do Povo (13 November) reports a Federal Police inquiry opened on 10 November and that hackers emailed APS seeking contact, unanswered. ABC do ABC (18 November) says more than 30 systems still run in alternative mode; APS cites a power failure then an intrusion that erased data, and says no confidential data leaked and cargo handling was never compromised.
title: Santos port authority systems still partly down after 6 November cyberattack; Federal Police investigating

validation.note: Follow-up read Gazeta do Povo (13 Nov) and ABC do ABC (18 Nov): both report a Federal Police investigation (Gazeta: inquiry opened 10 Nov), which settles the earlier conflict with Baguete (10 Nov, none yet). Attack and outage reported by Baguete, Gazeta do Povo, ABC do ABC and O POVO.
